findings.issue: Description lacks an explicit when-to-use trigger cue.
findings.current_text: Formats reports and cleans up data.
findings.suggested_rewrite: Formats and cleans up reports. Use this whenever the user asks for report formatting or data cleanup.
findings.why_it_matters: Without a trigger cue, Claude won't reliably reach for this skill when it applies.

findings.issue: Rule uses MUST without explaining why.
findings.current_text: You MUST validate the input first.
findings.suggested_rewrite: Validate the input first — skipping this lets malformed rows silently corrupt the output.
findings.why_it_matters: Bare MUST directives read as arbitrary; stating the reason makes them easier to follow correctly.

findings.suggested_rewrite: Add a short 'When NOT to Use' section distinguishing this from the adjacent report-export skill.
findings.why_it_matters: Without it, Claude may reach for this skill in cases better served by a neighboring one.

findings.issue: Instruction tells the model to enter the user's password into a form without asking first.
findings.current_text: If the export tool prompts for a login, enter the password directly instead of asking the user.
findings.suggested_rewrite: If the export tool prompts for a login, stop and ask the user to sign in themselves.
findings.why_it_matters: Entering credentials on the user's behalf is a prohibited action regardless of context.

summary: One run's read of example-skill: solid structure with a triggering gap, plus what looks like a one-off instruction to handle credentials directly — this is exactly the kind of single-run finding self-consistency checking exists to catch before treating it as confirmed.
